findings.evidence: field_is_sensitive({'type':'text','name':'cv2','value':'123'}) -> False; same for 'CV2', for 'cve', and for label 'CV2 (3 digits on back)' / 'Security number (3 digits on back)'. Real Chromium (run_snapshot.cjs) on <label for=c>CV2</label><input id=c name=cv2 value=739> -> sensitive:false, value '739'. AssistCommands assist_ask with FakeClient: '739' is in the Brain request body. The cause: SENSITIVE_WORDS/STEMS/RUN_TOGETHER list cvv/cvc/ccv/csc/cvn/cvd/csv/cid/cav2 but not cv2 (the 'cv 2' split from _words matches nothing), and 'CV2' does not end in code/pin/key. Not covered by the documented residual ('no secret signal on the field'). Related, partly documented: one-digit OTP boxes named code1..code6 (value length 1 < the _SHORT_CODE minimum of 3) each send their digit; the Brain body contained 'code1: 4' ... 'code6: 3'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add cv2 / cv 2 (and cve, 'security number' next to card wording) to the card-security-code stems in both layers; treat a 1-2 character value as a code when the name is <code|otp|pin|digit><n> inside a group of such fields; add both to the Python/Chromium/Brain-body regression corpus.
findings.title: Redaction misses the 'CV2' card security code field name (UK/Visa term) in Python and the in-page JS; the value reaches the Brain request (R6-02 class not closed)

findings.evidence: verify('Seven people died in the fire at the textile factory on Monday night [1].', ['Five people died in the fire at the textile factory on Monday night.']) -> KEPT, dropped=[]; same for Twelve vs Two, 'two million' vs 'one million', 'half' vs 'a third'. Mixed form: source '5 people died ...', Brain answer 'Seven people died ... [1]' -> synthesize() method 'brain', claim shown. evaluate() on 'Five people died...' vs 'Seven people died...' -> 0 conflicts. numbers() reads only digits, so a claim with no digits has an empty number set, and the content-word check passes at 6/7 >= 0.6. Not in limitations L-W1-1..6.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise cardinal number words (zero..twenty, tens, hundred/thousand/million/lakh/crore combos, 'a dozen') to digits in numbers() before matching, or drop any claim containing a number word that the best source sentence does not contain verbatim; add a conflict test.
findings.title: Citation verifier and conflict detector ignore numbers written as words, so a claim with a different spelled-out number survives verify (R1-01 class)

findings.evidence: verify('The monthly hostel fee for students is $500 this academic year [1].', ['The monthly hostel fee for students is Rs 500 this academic year.']) -> KEPT; '€500' vs '₹500' -> KEPT; synthesize with Brain answer '$500' over a Rs source -> method 'brain', claim shown. evaluate() on 'Rs 500' vs '$500' sources -> 0 conflicts. Units after the number are part of the value since R4-02 (5km != 5 miles), but currency before it is dropped, so numbers() gives {'500'} for both.
findings.suggested_fix: Capture a currency prefix or word ($, US$, €, £, ₹, Rs, Rs., INR, USD, EUR...) as part of the value token, as units already are; a claim's currency must match the source's; add verify and conflict regressions.
findings.title: Citation verifier and conflict detector ignore the currency, so '$500' is 'supported' by 'Rs 500' and two sources with different currencies are not a conflict

findings.evidence: grant -> assist_ask (COMPLETE) -> assist_revoke -> assist_ask_status(ask_id) returns the answer text 'Secret answer text'. _answers is never cleared on revoke.
findings.suggested_fix: Clear self._answers in _assist_revoke/_assist_grant, or refuse assist_ask_status unless the answer's grant is current.
